result.abstract: The lecture covers the muscles of facial expression, which are subcutaneous, insert into skin and are supplied by the facial nerve, group by group with their attachments, actions and the facial nerve branch that supplies them. It then covers the four muscles of mastication, supplied by the mandibular nerve, and the temporomandibular joint: its disc, ligaments, movements and dislocation.

concepts.name: Muscle of facial expression
concepts.definition: Thin subcutaneous muscle lying in the superficial fascia, arising from bone or fascia and inserting into skin. These muscles control facial expression and act as sphincters and dilators of the eyes, nose and mouth.

evidence.quote: They are subcutaneous, lying in the superficial fascia, with origins from bone or fascia and insertions into the skin.
Act as sphincters and dilators of the orifices of the face.

concepts.name: Muscle of mastication
concepts.definition: Thick muscle attached to bone that moves the mandible at the temporomandibular joint. There are four: temporalis, masseter, lateral pterygoid and medial pterygoid.

evidence.quote: Muscles of mastication: thick, attached to bone, supplied by the mandibular nerve (V3).
Four muscles of mastication: temporalis, masseter, lateral pterygoid, medial pterygoid.

concepts.name: Facial nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve VII, which supplies all the muscles of facial expression. It leaves the skull at the stylomastoid foramen, enters the parotid gland and divides into five terminal branches.

evidence.quote: All of them are supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII).
The facial nerve leaves the skull at the stylomastoid foramen, enters the parotid gland and forms the parotid plexus, which divides into the five terminal branches.

concepts.name: Mandibular nerve
concepts.definition: The V3 division of the trigeminal nerve, which supplies all four muscles of mastication.

evidence.quote: Four muscles, all supplied by the mandibular nerve (V3).

concepts.name: Trigeminal nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve that follows the first pharyngeal arch; through V3 it supplies the muscles of mastication.

evidence.quote: The muscles of mastication develop from the first arch, which follows the trigeminal nerve, so they take V3.

concepts.name: Oculomotor nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve III, which supplies the levator palpebrae superioris.

evidence.quote: Raises the upper eyelid. Nerve: oculomotor (CN III), not CN VII
Levator palpebrae superioris is the odd one out: CN III.

evidence.quote: Eyelid | Orbicularis oculi, corrugator supercilii, levator palpebrae superioris
Mouth | Orbicularis oris, buccinator, and the upper and lower groups of oral muscles

notes: Slides 37, 38 and 42 (tables of the muscles of mastication) are largely unreadable in the OCR; evidence for those muscles is taken from the summary section, exam points and flashcards.

Depressor anguli oris and depressor labii inferioris are only named (lower group, marginal mandibular branch), so they are described inside 'Lower group of oral muscles' rather than given their own concepts.
hy:9 also contrasts Bell's palsy with stroke (upper motor neuron, forehead spared); no separate concept was made for the stroke pattern.
The facial nerve branch table lists 'zygomaticus' under the buccal branch without saying major or minor; relations to zygomaticus major and minor use the per-muscle rows of the mouth table instead.
Movements of the mandible are linked to the temporomandibular joint with located-in (upper or lower part of the joint), as no closer relation type exists.
The relations of the TMJ (card m32) name neighbouring structures only in passing; they were not made into concepts.
